# Homelab Mini-PC / SFF Idle-Power & Virtualization-Fit Dataset

An open, cited dataset of the facts that decide which mini-PC or small server to buy for a homelab — the facts manufacturers **don't** print:

- **Measured idle watts** (wall power, *not* TDP)
- **ECC** memory support (and where it's only *claimed*, not verified)
- **NIC chipset** — Intel i226-V vs the buggy i225-V vs Realtek vs rock-solid Intel I219
- **RAM ceiling** (and soldered vs SODIMM)
- **IOMMU / GPU passthrough** behaviour (community reports)
- **AMD reset-bug** status for VFIO passthrough

**Every deciding field carries a dated source link, or is omitted.** No field is ever asserted without a citation — a wrong idle-watt or passthrough claim costs a buyer a $200–800 mistake.

➡️ **Browse it as a filterable finder: <https://idlewatt.vercel.app>**

---

## Why this exists

Ask HN, [May 2024](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40360255): *"Is there a site or database of mini pc's that I could use to attempt to pick one for homelab usage? ... no easy way to compare specs and price other than spending hours reading reviews for each of them."*

There still isn't a single crowd-sourced, searchable database for the number that actually matters: **measured idle power**. Spec sheets list **TDP**, which is a thermal-design rating for sizing a cooler — *not* a power-draw figure. The same chassis with a 35 W-TDP "T" chip vs a 65 W-TDP desktop chip idles ~11 W vs ~18 W. For an always-on box every watt of idle is roughly **$1/year (US)** or **$2.50/year (EU)**.

The data exists — but scattered across one-off forum posts, a German Google Doc of sub-30W builds, individual blog wall-meter readings, and Proxmox-forum passthrough war stories. This repo aggregates those measurements into one machine-readable place, with the source for every claim.

## Quick answers (money questions)

- **What's the lowest-idle homelab mini-PC?** Fanless N100 boxes (Minisforum UN100C ~5–7 W) and a tuned used Intel NUC (~8.7 W week-average) sit at the bottom. See the [finder sorted by idle](https://idlewatt.vercel.app).
- **i225-V or i226-V?** The **i226-V** — the i225-V has a documented random-dropout bug that takes a headless box offline until a hard reset. Many cheap boxes ship Realtek RTL8125 (Linux-only, occasional dropouts).
- **Which mini-PC supports ECC?** Almost none of the consumer N100/Ryzen boxes. AMD Ryzen PRO APUs (Lenovo M75q) are the usual "maybe" — and the community never validated a specific working ECC SODIMM, so we mark it **unverified**. Real ECC means a Xeon-E tower at ~10× the idle power.
- **Why is iGPU passthrough hard on the Minisforum MS-01?** The Iris Xe iGPU exposes multiple functions; full passthrough is notoriously fiddly. **SR-IOV vGPU** is the reliable route for Plex/Jellyfin transcode.
- **AMD reset bug?** AMD APU GPUs work on first VM boot but won't reset on restart until the host reboots — unless you install [gnif's vendor-reset](https://github.com/gnif/vendor-reset) (and even that doesn't cover every APU).

## Data

- [`data/models.json`](data/models.json) — the full structured dataset (each field: `{ value, source: { title, url, date } }`).
- [`data/models.csv`](data/models.csv) — flattened, one row per model, with a source URL column per field.

51 models across N100/N150 new-wave mini-PCs, multi-NIC router boards (CWWK/Topton), virtualization SFF (MS-01), AMD Ryzen mini-PCs, Intel NUCs, used enterprise 1L (Lenovo Tiny / Dell OptiPlex Micro / HP EliteDesk Mini), and a tower-server reference point.

## Methodology

The binding rule: **cited or omitted**. A value with a dated third-party source, or blank — never a bare assertion. Idle figures note the method (Kill-A-Watt, smart-plug week average, iDRAC) and the caveat that draw varies with OS, 120 V vs 240 V mains, and `powertop` tuning. `proxmox_fit` is an editorial verdict *derived from* the cited fields and is labelled as such, not presented as a spec.

Full source list + per-field methodology: <https://idlewatt.vercel.app/methodology>

## Contributing

Corrections and new wall-meter measurements are welcome as PRs — that's the point: turn scattered community readings into one queryable place. Please include a source link and the measurement method for any number.

## License

Data released under **CC BY 4.0** — reuse it, just keep the attribution. Source citations belong to their respective authors.
